title: Unitary Method
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Unitary Method. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
One unit, then the required units

The unitary method finds the value or rate for one unit and scales it to the required amount. If 8 metres cost ₹560, one metre costs ₹70 and 13 metres cost ₹910, provided the price per metre is constant. State the unit at every step so rupees per metre is not confused with metres per rupee.

Direct and inverse variation

In direct proportion, the ratio of corresponding quantities is constant: doubling one doubles the other. In inverse proportion, their product is constant: doubling one halves the other. Work-and-time problems are inverse only when worker efficiency and conditions remain unchanged. For compound situations, change one quantity at a time and decide whether the relationship is direct or inverse.

Worked example: Eight workers finish a job in 15 days. At the same rate, 12 workers need (\(8 × 15/12=10\)) days. The total work is 120 worker-days.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Write the one-unit rate with its units before scaling.
  • Ask whether more of the first quantity means more or less of the second before choosing direct or inverse proportion.
  • For several changing quantities, use a ratio table and label each relationship.
  • Check whether the problem justifies a constant rate.
  • Convert units before comparing rates such as metres per second and kilometres per hour.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Direct proportion: y/x is constant.
  • Inverse proportion: xy is constant.
  • Work = rate × time; for identical workers, worker-days can remain constant.
  • Unitary steps require an unchanged rate or proportional relationship.
  • Include requested units in the final answer.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    Eight metres of cloth cost ₹560. What is the cost of 13 metres at the same rate?

    1. ₹840
    2. ₹910
    3. ₹980
    4. ₹1,040
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: ₹910

    One metre costs (\(560/8=₹70\)). Thus 13 metres cost (\(13\cdot70=₹910\)).

  2. Core:

    Five identical machines make 400 parts in an hour. At the same rate, how many parts do eight machines make in an hour?

    1. (\(560\))
    2. (\(600\))
    3. (\(640\))
    4. (\(800\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(640\))

    One machine makes (\(400/5=80\)) parts per hour. Eight make (\(8\cdot80=640\)).

  3. Foundation:

    Twelve books cost ₹540 at a constant price. What do 7 books cost?

    1. ₹280
    2. ₹315
    3. ₹350
    4. ₹378
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: ₹315

    One book costs (\(540/12=₹45\)). Seven cost (\(7 × ₹45=₹315\)).

  4. Standard:

    Eight workers complete a job in 15 days. How many days do 12 equally efficient workers need?

    1. (\(8 days\))
    2. (\(10 days\))
    3. (\(12 days\))
    4. (\(22.5 days\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(10 days\))

    Work is constant: (\(8 × 15=120\)) worker-days. Time is (\(120/12=10\)) days.

  5. Challenge:

    Three identical pumps fill a tank in 8 hours. How long would four pumps take under the same conditions?

    1. (\(4 h\))
    2. (\(6 h\))
    3. (\(8 h\))
    4. (\(10 h\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(6 h\))

    Pump count and time are inversely proportional: (\(3 × 8=4t\)), so (\(t=6\)) hours.
